age.notes: Values are cohort mean ages (subgroup-level aggregate), not individual subject ages.

age_group.evidence_quote: 23 adults... 25 children... 24 adults... 26 infants... 37 adults... 31 children
age_group.notes: Age group labels as used verbatim by authors (adults, children, infants); Ghana/Tanzania 'children' subgroups include a wide age range (0-15/0-18 yrs) that may span Infant/Child/Adolescent categories.

family.evidence_quote: In Ghana 12 extended families... 18 families from Korogwe District... This cohort included 24 mothers and their infant(s)
family.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
family.notes: Family counts reported (12 in Ghana, 18 in Tanzania, 24 mother-infant pairs in Ethiopia) but no individual family identifiers given in main text.

family_role.evidence_quote: This cohort included 24 mothers and their infant(s) for a total of 50 metagenomes.
family_role.section: Method Details — Westernisation and Additional Non-Westernized Datasets
family_role.notes: Ghana and Tanzania described as 'extended families' without specifying mother/father/child roles per subgroup.

sex.notes: Ghana adults reported as 52.2% female/47.8% male and Tanzania adults 48.65% female/51.35% male (mixed-sex aggregate, cannot be reduced to a single enum value); Ghana/Tanzania children and Ethiopia infants sex not reported.

zigosity.notes: No twin/zygosity information reported in this paper.

age_min.notes: Overall 'value' is the minimum age across all reported subgroup ranges (Ghana/Ethiopia/Tanzania adults, children, infants). Per-subgroup ranges are directly stated in text.

age_max.notes: Overall 'value' is the maximum age across all reported subgroup ranges. Per-subgroup ranges are directly stated in text.

age_years.notes: Only mean age with s.d. and range reported per subgroup, not a single specific age; means: Ghana adults 33.14, Ghana children 6.81, Ethiopia adults 29.35, Ethiopia infants 1.31, Tanzania adults 29.27, Tanzania children 8.22.

bmi.notes: BMI mentioned as a factor considered for clade association but no values reported for participants of this study; only referenced as 'Table S1' for other cohorts.

dietary_restriction.notes: No specific dietary restriction/regime reported for individual participants; only general dietary lifestyle descriptions (non-Westernized diet).

disease.evidence_quote: All individuals sampled in this study were healthy defined as free of self-reported disease.
disease.notes: Applies uniformly to the Ghana, Ethiopia, and Tanzania cohorts newly sequenced in this study. Other diseases (CRC, T2D, hypertension, liver cirrhosis, IBD) were analyzed only via publicly available external datasets in a secondary meta-analysis, without participant-level demographic data reported in this paper, so not extracted as participant-level disease values.

disease_details.notes: No further disease detail beyond 'healthy' reported for study participants.

feces_phenotype.notes: No stool phenotype/clinical stool measurement reported.

fmt_id.notes: No FMT (fecal microbiota transplantation) study design reported.

neonatal_feeding_method.notes: Not reported, though infants were sampled in Ethiopia (paired infant-mother samples); feeding method not described.

obgyn_lactating.notes: Not reported, though mothers of sampled infants are mentioned; lactation status not described.

treatment.notes: No participant treatment/medication reported; this is a microbiome genomics study, not an interventional clinical trial.

tumor_staging_ajcc.notes: Not reported; CRC datasets referenced are external publicly available cohorts without patient-level staging data provided in this paper.

biomarker_name.notes: No clinical biomarker panel reported; paper focuses on genomic/microbial diversity analyses.

disease_response_os.notes: Study is a microbial genomics/metagenomics analysis, not a clinical survival study.

ecog_performance_status.notes: No ECOG or clinical performance status data reported.

feces_phenotype_value.notes: No feces phenotype scoring (e.g., Bristol stool scale) reported.

tumor_size_measurement.notes: No tumor size measurements reported; disease association analyses used prevalence/abundance of P. copri clades, not tumor sizes.

value: Ghana cohort: 44 individuals (23 adults, avg age 33.14 yrs (s.d. 6.61), range 20-45, 52.2% female; 25 children, avg age 6.81 yrs (s.d. 3.67), range 0-15 yrs)
Ethiopia cohort: 50 individuals (24 adults, avg age 29.35 yrs (s.d. 6.24), range 22-45, 100% female; 26 infants, avg age 1.31 yrs (s.d. 1.05), range 0.167-4.5 yrs)
Tanzania cohort: 68 individuals (37 adults, avg age 29.27 yrs (s.d. 8.88), range 18-61, 48.65% female; 31 children, avg age 8.22 yrs (s.d. 4.74), range 0-18 yrs)
6,874 publicly available metagenomes from 36 individual datasets, representing six continents and 25 different countries
1,023 total P. copri genomes reconstructed (17 isolates, 1,006 MAGs)
P. copri complex comprises four clades (A, B, C, D) with >10% inter-clade ANI divergence
Non-Westernized population P. copri prevalence: 95.4%; Westernized population prevalence: 29.6%
Clade prevalence in non-Westernized vs Westernized: A 91.5% vs 26.9%; C 88.2% vs 8.35%; B 73.5% vs 6.2%; D 68.8% vs 2.7%
Ancient samples analyzed: Iceman (5,300-year-old ice mummy) and three Mexican coprolites (~1,300 ± 100 BP)
Divergence estimate: P. copri began to diversify (clade B split) ~6.5 million years ago; clades A, D, C diversified ~3.5-2.5 million years ago

extraction_warnings: Only aggregate (subgroup-level) demographic statistics are reported in the main text for the three newly sequenced cohorts (Ghana, Ethiopia, Tanzania); no individual subject_id or sample_id values are available.
Detailed per-sample metadata is stated to reside in Supplementary Tables S1, S2, and S5, which were not included in the provided paper content, so sample_level granularity could not be produced.
For fields describing mixed-sex subgroups (Ghana adults, Tanzania adults), the enum 'sex' field cannot represent a percentage split and was marked not_reported with details in notes.
study_name was inferred/constructed since no canonical study identifier was explicitly stated in the text.

The overall study also includes numerous public disease cohorts (CRC, T2D, hypertension, liver cirrhosis, IBD) analyzed via meta-analysis, but these were not described with subject-level demographic data in the provided text and were excluded from subgroup extraction.

This paper is a microbiome genomics/population-structure study (Prevotella copri), not a clinical cohort study; most clinical/lifestyle schema fields (zygosity, antibiotics, BMI, dietary restriction, disease response, HLA, neonatal/obstetric variables, smoking, treatment, tumor staging) are not reported for study participants.

Demographic data (age, country, life-stage group) are only available for the newly sequenced Ghana, Ethiopia, and Tanzania cohorts described in 'Experimental Model and Subject Details'; these were stratified into subgroups by country and age-group (adults/children/infants).
age_min and age_max top-level 'value' fields are derived as the overall min/max across all reported subgroups; per-subgroup values reflect the directly stated ranges in the text.

Disease status 'Healthy' applies only to the newly sequenced Ghana/Ethiopia/Tanzania participants; disease association analyses (CRC, T2D, hypertension, liver cirrhosis, IBD) used external publicly available datasets without participant-level demographic/clinical data reported in this paper, so were not extracted as participant records.

Supplementary tables (Table S1, S2, S4, S5) likely contain additional per-sample metadata (e.g., age, BMI, disease, country) but their content was not provided in the extracted text, so sample-level extraction was not possible.

This paper is a microbial genomics/metagenomics study of Prevotella copri, not a clinical trial or biomarker study; most schema fields (biomarker, OS, ECOG, tumor size, feces phenotype) are not applicable and were marked not_reported.
The 'feces_phenotype_value' field has no corresponding 'feces_phenotype' name field in the schema, making its intended scope ambiguous; treated as not_reported.
